title: Mathematical Language & Proofs
description: Notation, quantifiers, definition–theorem–proof and first proof techniques.
html:
📝 Mathematical Language & Proofs

1. Statements and implications

$$\neg A, \quad A \land B, \quad A \lor B, \quad A \Rightarrow B, \quad A \Leftrightarrow B$$

$A \Rightarrow B$ is false only when $A$ is true and $B$ is false.

Related statements

The contrapositive $\neg B \Rightarrow \neg A$ is equivalent to $A \Rightarrow B$. The converse $B \Rightarrow A$ is not.

$A$ sufficient for $B$, $B$ necessary for $A$. de Morgan: $\neg(A \land B) = \neg A \lor \neg B$.

2. Quantifiers and sets

$$\neg(\forall x: P(x)) \iff \exists x: \neg P(x), \qquad \neg(\exists x: P(x)) \iff \forall x: \neg P(x)$$

The order matters: $\forall x \exists y: y > x$ is true, $\exists y \forall x: y > x$ is false.

$$A = B \iff A \subset B \text{ and } B \subset A$$

3. Proof techniques

  • Direct: assumption → insert definition → transform → claim
  • Contrapositive: prove $\neg B \Rightarrow \neg A$
  • Contradiction: assume the opposite, derive a contradiction (e.g. $\sqrt{2}$ irrational)
  • Counterexample: refute a universal statement with one example
  • Induction: base case $n = 1$ and step $k \to k + 1$

Typical mistakes

  • Examples do not replace a proof
  • Confusing the converse with the contrapositive
  • Circular reasoning, division by $0$
